lessons.title: Excel Basics and Cell References

content.title: Excel Basics
content.text: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application used to store, organize, calculate and analyze data.

content.title: Workbook and Worksheet
content.text: A workbook is an Excel file that can contain multiple worksheets. A worksheet contains rows and columns of cells.

content.title: Cell References
content.text: A cell reference identifies a cell using its column letter and row number, such as A1 or C5.

content.title: Relative and Absolute References
content.text: Relative references change when a formula is copied. Absolute references use $ to keep a row or column fixed, such as $A$1.

key_points: A workbook can contain multiple worksheets.
Cells are identified using column letters and row numbers.

content.title: Functions
content.text: Excel functions are predefined formulas that perform calculations on data.

lessons.title: Logical Functions and Conditional Analysis

content.title: IF Function
content.text: The IF function returns one result when a condition is true and another result when it is false.

content.title: Conditional Analysis
content.text: Logical functions are useful for classification, validation and rule-based analysis.

key_points: AND requires all conditions to be true.
OR requires at least one condition to be true.

lessons.title: Sorting, Filtering and Data Cleaning

content.title: Sorting
content.text: Sorting arranges data according to values, such as smallest to largest or alphabetically.

content.title: Filtering
content.text: Filtering temporarily displays only rows that satisfy selected conditions.

content.title: Remove Duplicates
content.text: Excel provides a Remove Duplicates feature for identifying and removing repeated records.

content.title: Data Cleaning
content.text: Common cleaning tasks include removing duplicates, handling missing values, correcting inconsistent formats and standardizing text.

content.title: Find and Replace
content.text: Find and Replace can quickly locate specific values and replace them with corrected or standardized values.

key_points: Sorting changes the order of displayed records.
Cleaning improves data quality before analysis.

lessons.title: Lookup Functions

content.title: Lookup Functions
content.text: Lookup functions find information in a table based on a matching value.

content.title: Choosing a Lookup
content.text: XLOOKUP is a modern lookup function, while VLOOKUP is widely used in existing spreadsheets.

key_points: INDEX and MATCH can be combined for flexible lookups.

lessons.title: Charts and Data Visualization

content.title: Why Use Charts?
content.text: Charts convert numerical data into visual representations that can make patterns and comparisons easier to understand.

content.title: Column and Bar Charts
content.text: Column and bar charts are useful for comparing values across categories.

content.title: Line Charts
content.text: Line charts are useful for showing trends over time.

content.title: Pie Charts
content.text: Pie charts can show the relative contribution of categories to a whole, particularly when there are few categories.

content.title: Good Visualization
content.text: A useful chart should have an appropriate chart type, clear labels, meaningful titles and minimal unnecessary decoration.

key_points: Bar and column charts compare categories.
Chart selection should match the analytical question.

content.title: What is a PivotTable?
content.text: A PivotTable summarizes large datasets by grouping and aggregating values.

content.title: PivotTable Areas
content.text: The main areas are Rows, Columns, Values and Filters. Fields can be dragged into these areas to build a summary.

content.title: Aggregation
content.text: Values can be summarized using calculations such as Sum, Count and Average.

content.title: Example
content.text: A sales dataset can be summarized by placing Region in Rows and Sales in Values to calculate sales by region.

content.title: PivotCharts
content.text: PivotCharts provide visual representations of PivotTable summaries and can help explore aggregated data.
